## Abstract

Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of childhood morbidity, however there is no systematic testing in children hospitalised with respiratory symptoms. Therefore, current RSV incidence likely underestimates the true burden. We used probabilistically linked perinatal, hospital, and laboratory records of 321,825 children born in Western Australia (WA), 2000–2012. We generated a predictive model for RSV positivity in hospitalised children aged < 5 years. We applied the model to all hospitalisations in our population-based cohort to determine the true RSV incidence, and under-ascertainment fraction. The model’s predictive performance was determined using cross-validated area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC) curve**.** From 321,825 hospitalisations, 37,784 were tested for RSV (22.8% positive). Predictors of RSV positivity included younger admission age, male sex, non-Aboriginal ethnicity, a diagnosis of bronchiolitis and longer hospital stay. Our model showed good predictive accuracy (AUROC: 0.87). The respective sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value and negative predictive values were 58.4%, 92.2%, 68.6% and 88.3%. The predicted incidence rates of hospitalised RSV for children aged < 3 months was 43.7/1000 child-years (95% CI 42.1–45.4) compared with 31.7/1000 child-years (95% CI 30.3–33.1) from laboratory-confirmed RSV admissions. Findings from our study suggest that the true burden of RSV may be 30–57% higher than current estimates.

## Introduction

Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in young children worldwide, causing 3.2 million detected hospitalisation episodes every year[1](/articles/s41598-021-04080-3#ref-CR1 "Shi, T. et al. Global, regional, and national disease burden estimates of acute lower respiratory infections due to respiratory syncytial virus in young children in 2015: a systematic review and modelling study. The Lancet 390, 946–958 (2017)."). The true burden is likely to be much greater, with approximately half of RSV-associated deaths estimated to occur outside of hospital[1](/articles/s41598-021-04080-3#ref-CR1 "Shi, T. et al. Global, regional, and national disease burden estimates of acute lower respiratory infections due to respiratory syncytial virus in young children in 2015: a systematic review and modelling study. The Lancet 390, 946–958 (2017)."). In Australia, for every 100,000 hospitalised children aged < 5 years, an estimated 418 have RSV[2](/articles/s41598-021-04080-3#ref-CR2 "Saravanos, G. L. et al. Respiratory syncytial virus-associated hospitalisations in Australia, 2006–2015. Med. J. Aust. 210, 447–453 (2019)."). A recent population-based study in Western Australia (WA) conducted by our group reported pathogen-specific incidence rates of 247/100,000 child-years for RSV in children aged < 17 years[3](/articles/s41598-021-04080-3#ref-CR3 "Lim, F. J., Blyth, C. C., Fathima, P., de Klerk, N. & Moore, H. C. Record linkage study of the pathogen-specific burden of respiratory viruses in children. Influenza Other Respir. Viruses 11, 502–510 (2017)."), with the highest burden among infants in their first 3 months of life (28.1/1000 child-years)[4](/articles/s41598-021-04080-3#ref-CR4 "Moore, H. C. et al. Assessing the burden of laboratory-confirmed respiratory syncytial virus infection in a population cohort of Australian children through record linkage. J. Infect. Dis. 2, 106 (2020)."). RSV is most frequently associated with hospitalisations for acute bronchiolitis, but was also identified across other clinical diagnoses including pneumonia, unspecified acute lower respiratory infections, asthma, upper respiratory infections as well as non-specific viral diagnosis codes[3](/articles/s41598-021-04080-3#ref-CR3 "Lim, F. J., Blyth, C. C., Fathima, P., de Klerk, N. & Moore, H. C. Record linkage study of the pathogen-specific burden of respiratory viruses in children. Influenza Other Respir. Viruses 11, 502–510 (2017)."),[5](/articles/s41598-021-04080-3#ref-CR5 "Müller-Pebody, B., Edmunds, W., Zambon, M., Gay, N. & Crowcroft, N. Contribution of RSV to bronchiolitis and pneumonia-associated hospitalizations in English children, April 1995–March 1998. Epidemiol. Infect. 129, 99–106 (2002).").

Population-wide in our jurisdiction and elsewhere, there is no systematic approach to RSV testing, nor is it currently a notifiable disease, making estimates of RSV disease burden using microbiological testing datasets alone difficult. From our population-based study, only 10% of children aged < 17 years were ever tested for RSV and variable testing trends were seen between age groups and from year to year. Additionally, 54% of children hospitalised with respiratory infections did not have a corresponding microbiological test[3](/articles/s41598-021-04080-3#ref-CR3 "Lim, F. J., Blyth, C. C., Fathima, P., de Klerk, N. & Moore, H. C. Record linkage study of the pathogen-specific burden of respiratory viruses in children. Influenza Other Respir. Viruses 11, 502–510 (2017)."). Improved estimates of RSV burden are required to inform future policy for RSV therapeutics and preventative strategies, as late-stage clinical trials of antivirals, maternal vaccines and monoclonal antibodies progress[3](/articles/s41598-021-04080-3#ref-CR3 "Lim, F. J., Blyth, C. C., Fathima, P., de Klerk, N. & Moore, H. C. Record linkage study of the pathogen-specific burden of respiratory viruses in children. Influenza Other Respir. Viruses 11, 502–510 (2017)."),[6](/articles/s41598-021-04080-3#ref-CR6 "Griffin, M. P. et al. Single-dose nirsevimab for prevention of RSV in preterm infants. N. Engl. J. Med. 383, 415–425 (2020).").

Understanding the demographic and clinical predictors of RSV test positivity in different populations can aid in quantifying the under-ascertainment burden of RSV from standalone datasets. Ideally, a combination of clinical and laboratory data is needed. Such a study has been conducted in England for infants aged < 1 year, using hospitalisation data and RSV positive testing records[7](/articles/s41598-021-04080-3#ref-CR7 "Reeves, R. et al. Burden of hospital admissions caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in infants in England: a data linkage modelling study. J. Infect. 78, 468–475 (2019).").

The aim of our study was to develop a prediction model to estimate the true incidence of RSV associated hospitalisations in children < 5 years of age in WA and to use these findings to determine the under-ascertainment fraction of RSV incidence using laboratory records alone.

## Methods

### Setting and data sources

WA covers the western third of Australia with a population of approximately 2.6 million people at 31 December 2019[8](/articles/s41598-021-04080-3#ref-CR8 "Australian Bureau of Statistics. Australian Demographic Statistics,

## Abstract

Training in working memory tasks is associated with lasting changes in prefrontal cortical activity. To assess the neural activity changes induced by training, we recorded single units, multi-unit activity (MUA) and local field potentials (LFP) with chronic electrode arrays implanted in the prefrontal cortex of two monkeys, throughout the period they were trained to perform cognitive tasks. Mastering different task phases was associated with distinct changes in neural activity, which included recruitment of larger numbers of neurons, increases or decreases of their firing rate, changes in the correlation structure between neurons, and redistribution of power across LFP frequency bands. In every training phase, changes induced by the actively learned task were also observed in a control task, which remained the same across the training period. Our results reveal how learning to perform cognitive tasks induces plasticity of prefrontal cortical activity, and how activity changes may generalize between tasks.

**Subject terms:** Cognitive control, Working memory

---

It remains unclear whether improvements in one cognitive task transfer to other tasks. Here, the authors show that changes in prefrontal neuronal activation, firing rate, and local field potentials induced during active learning of a working memory task are also evident in a control task.

## Introduction

Working memory, the ability to retain and manipulate information over a period of seconds, represents a core component of higher cognitive functions, including control of attention, non-verbal reasoning, and academic performance[1](#CR1)–[3](#CR3). Working memory ability has been traditionally thought of as an immutable aptitude, but it is now understood that it can be improved by training in working memory tasks[4](#CR4)–[6](#CR6). The extent over which performance improvement after working memory training generalizes, or transfers, to tasks that were not part of the training has been a matter of debate; some studies have been successful in inducing transfer from one task to another whereas others have not[4](#CR4)–[11](#CR11). Less contested is the idea that working memory training is beneficial for patients with clinical conditions, including attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), traumatic brain injury, and schizophrenia[4](#CR4),[12](#CR12),[13](#CR13).

The neural basis of transfer has been poorly understood. Human fMRI studies have produced conflicting results about the effects of cognitive training, suggesting overall increases[13](#CR13)–[18](#CR18), or decreases in activity[19](#CR19)–[22](#CR22), or more subtle differences such as changes in network modularity[23](#CR23),[24](#CR24). Increases are interpreted as reflecting a higher level of activation or recruitment of a larger cortical area, decreases as suggestive of improvements in efficiency[25](#CR25),[26](#CR26). What these correspond to at the level of neural spiking activity and how lasting changes can transfer between tasks has been hitherto unexplained.

We were thus motivated to address the neural effects of training in a spatial working memory task that with neurophysiological recordings in monkeys. Persistent discharges that continue to represent stimulus properties are thought to underlie working memory, though this is a topic of recent debate, as well[27](#CR27),[28](#CR28). We standardized the training in discrete phases and tracked neuronal activity with a chronically implanted electrode array throughout several months of training. We were thus able to address changes in neuronal activity as training proceeded and test how neural activity changes were evident across different tasks.

## Results

### Monkeys acquire different elements of cognitive tasks with training

Two male Rhesus monkeys (*Macaca mulatta*) were initially acclimated with the laboratory and trained to maintain fixation and not respond to stimuli presented on a computer screen. The monkeys were then trained to perform a spatial working memory task, requiring them to maintain fixation, observe two stimuli appearing in sequence separated by delay periods, and to indicate if the two stimuli appeared at the same location or not by selecting one of two choice targets, defined by their shape (“H” or “Diamond” in Fig. [1a–e](#Fig1)). The training to acquire and master this task consisted of four phases. First, the monkey was presented with two stimuli in rapid succession and had to indicate if they appeared at the same or different locations by selecting one of two choice targets (Fig. [1b](#Fig1)). During this phase, daily sessions involved the presentation of the cue at the right of the fixation point followed by a sample stimulus appearing at either a matching location (right) or a nonmatching location (left), on different days. At this stage, the monkey could simply sample the choice targets, determine which one was rewarded during the block, and repeatedly select it in following trials. In the second phase, the monkey was presented with alternating blocks of match and nonmatch trials, of decreasing block length, until they were randomly interleaved, requiring the monkey to associate the second stimulus location with the corresponding choice target (Fig. [1c](#Fig1)). In the third phase, the monkey had to generalize the task to new stimulus locations, appearing at a 3 × 3 grid (Fig. [1d](#Fig1)). Finally, an increasing delay period was imposed, placing more demand on working memory (Fig. [1e](#Fig1)).

**a–e** Successive frames illustrate the sequence of events in the tasks used in progressing training phases. **a** During the pre-training phase, the monkey only had to fixate while the stimuli were displayed at any one of the nine locations on the screen. **b** In Phase I, a stimulus was always presented to the right, followed by a match stimulus in a block of trials and by a nonmatch stimulus in another block of trials. At the end of the trial, two choice targets appeared, and the monkey had to choose the “Diamond” target in match blocks and the “H” target in nonmatch blocks to get a reward. **c** In Phase II, match and nonmatch trials were mixed in a block. **d** In Phase III, the stimulus location of the first stimulus could vary. **e** In Phase IV, the duration of the delay period increased. The passive stimulus set continued to be presented at the beginning of each session throughout training. **f**, **g** Performance of two monkeys at each daily session. Each dot represents one day’s performance. Red lines represent data averaged over 30 days.

Importantly, visual stimuli were also presented to the monkeys passively, in a control, fixation task every day (Fig. [1a](#Fig1)). The sequence of events in the passive trials mirrored the final phase of the active task; a stimulus was presented at a random location, followed by a second stimulus appearing either at a matching or a nonmatching location, separated by 1.5 s delay periods. The critical difference was that no choice targets were presented in the passive task, and the monkey was rewarded at the end of the second delay period merely for maintaining fixation; no response of any kind was required. The monkeys performed this passive fixation task before recordings began, and they continued to perform it in exactly the same fashion at the beginning of each daily session before active task training began. Training proceeded in an adaptive manner, so that the task became progressively harder as the monkeys mastered each element of the task so that overall performance remained approximately constant through the duration of the training (Fig. [1f, g](#Fig1)).

### Training increases neuronal activation

After initial acclimation with the laboratory and before Phase I training began, the animals were implanted with a chronic array of electrodes in their lateral prefrontal cortex (Fig. [2a](#Fig2)). The implant comprised an 8 × 8 grid of electrodes, with adjacent electrodes spaced 0.75 mm apart from each other, thus covering an area of 5.25 mm × 5.25 mm. The electrode array was implanted in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC), with electrode tracks descending in both banks of the principal sulcus (Fig. [2b, c](#Fig2)). Local field potentials (LFP) and multi-unit activity (MUA) were recorded from all electrodes, which remained fixed after training began. To sample spiking activity in an unbiased fashion, we set the exact same MUA threshold criterion for all electrodes and sessions, to 3.5 × root mean square (RMS) of the noise level. We were thus able to quantify systematic changes in neural activity as training took place. We identified MUA units with responsiveness to stimuli as those exhibiting a significant elevation of firing rate during either the first stimulus presentation or the delay period following it (see Methods). A total of 4537 responsive MUA units were identified in this fashion across all phases of training and across all electrodes, with a sustained yield of responsive units through the last training phase (Fig. [2d–f](#Fig2)). Single neuron recordings were also obtained, after spike sorting of the MUA records. A total of 1093 single units were recorded from the active task and 1065 from the passive task; of those 49.2% were responsive in the active task and 27.2% in the passive task, based on the same criteria.

## 1. Discussion（讨论）

**第 231 行 - 第 249 行：**

RSV vaccine development has gained substantial attention globally, with the WHO identifying global RSV disease burden estimates as a global priority. Our study aimed to improve the estimates of RSV incidence which are needed to help advocate for vaccine programs and provide essential baseline data to evaluate vaccine impact studies. Using population-based hospital and laboratory data, our results corroborated previous findings of the large burden of RSV-associated hospital admissions in children, and our prediction model suggests that we underestimate this burden by more than 30%. Over the study period, which spanned more than a decade, the burden of predicted RSV-associated hospital admissions was substantial, with an average annual estimated admission rate of 404 per 1000 children for < 3 months and 338 per 1000 children for under 2 years old respectively. This is consistent with our previous results and with findings from other studies.

Our analysis confirmed that children who are younger at admission (< 3 months) are at increased risk of RSV positivity, which is consistent with other studies. In addition to younger age, our study also identified additional important predictors of RSV positivity, including length of hospital stay, primary or secondary diagnosis of acute bronchiolitis, pneumonia, bronchitis and unspecified ALRIs. A primary or secondary diagnosis of acute bronchiolitis was the strongest predictor of RSV positivity. A diagnosis of bronchitis was the second most important predictor, followed by pneumonia. A previous study in England similarly reported that infants with a diagnosis of bronchiolitis, unspecified LRTI or with an RSV-specific code had higher odds of RSV-positivity.

The risk of hospitalisation was higher for non-Aboriginal children and children from a rural or remote region at birth. Similarly, the highest rates of RSV were found in remote and rural regions compared to metropolitan areas. These difference could be attributed to a combination of socio economic disadvantages (such as household crowding) and access to health care. Interestingly, low SES, prematurity and family history of asthma were associated with lower odds of RSV positivity. Similar findings were reported in previous studies. Nonetheless, findings reported elsewhere have suggested that the majority of cases with RSV do not have any underlying co-morbidity.

Our evaluation using tenfold cross validation showed an excellent performance and was well calibrated, with AUROC of 0.87. By comparison, in a recent study predicting RSV associated admissions in England reported AUROC of 0.9, our predictive model has higher specificity and NPV but lower sensitivity and PPV compared to that model which focused on infants under the age of 12 months. Our prediction study differs from others with respect to either the domain or population studied. Other studies focused on RSV hospitalisation in young children, premature infants, or non-hospitalised RSV among healthy term infants.

Our prediction model showed a good fit to the seasonality and age distribution of RSV-associated hospitalisation. However, the model slightly underestimated the RSV-associated admissions for older children. This could be due to non-inclusion of additional risk factors, or lifestyle factors beyond the perinatal period, where we had limited data to base our prediction model on. Our prediction model was based on more than a decade of population-based hospitalisation data linked with laboratory and socio-demographic records, which is a key strength of our study. Our model included a comprehensive list of maternal, infant, and perinatal predictors which were not included in previous similar RSV prediction studies. We also employed a DAG as an efficient strategy to improve predictor selection in the prediction modelling. We believe the definition of ALRIs, and other infections included as risk factors in our prediction model increases the likelihood of positive detection of a respiratory virus in hospital admissions. We also employed a k-fold cross validation, an internal validation method that takes over-optimism into account far better than conventional data splitting.

---

## 2. Limitations（研究局限性）

**第 245 行 - 第 246 行**（讨论部分内）：

Our study has some limitations. Firstly, our results are based on hospitalisation data linked to laboratory records with specimen collection within 48 h of hospital admission. Therefore, we are limiting our prediction model to more severe RSV cases associated with hospitalisation and therefore our model does not estimate the broader community incidence of RSV. Secondly, our analysis only included linked data in the years between 2000–2012, and more recent trends in hospital admissions are not reflected in our results. However, we are confident our model can be applied to more contemporary data and believe that the majority of the known perinatal and environmental predictors are not likely to change over time. Our study did not include other potential predictors such as breastfeeding, immunodeficiencies, day care attendance, and environmental factors, as these factors are not routinely collected in databases available for linkage. However, we do not expect a major underestimation of our prediction model as these variables are not known to be strong predictors of RSV associated admissions. Additionally, even though the testing detection method would not impact the propensity to get tested, our sensitivity analysis suggested that the prediction model performance slightly different by laboratory detection method.

The population-based linkage of routine laboratory and hospitalisation data allowed us to develop a predictive model with excellent predictive performance to identify RSV associated hospitalisation in WA. Applying the model to all hospitalised children aged less than 5 years (irrespective of respiratory infection diagnosis) during the study period enabled us to estimate the true RSV burden in hospitalised children in the state.

Further research is needed that takes into consideration emergency department and community RSV-associated admissions, preferably including recent data, as well as other potential predictors. A development of a simple risk score, and further external validation of the model in other populations must also be considered for possible future clinical use of the prediction model.

**第 251 行 - 第 253 行：**

We have successfully developed a prediction model using population-based data to estimate the true burden of RSV in hospitalised children in WA with good predictive performance and internal validation. Findings from our study indicate that the true burden of RSV is up to 30–57% higher than figures based solely on laboratory detection data in young children. These estimates can now be used as input parameters in dynamic transmission models to better predict the impact of prevention measures including maternal vaccination.

# 结构化科研正文（重写）

**基于原文**: Gebremedhin AT, Hogan AB, Blyth CC, Glass K, Moore HC. *Developing a prediction model to estimate the true burden of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in hospitalised children in Western Australia.* Scientific Reports, 2022;12:332.

- **DOI**: [10.1038/s41598-021-04080-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-021-04080-3)
- **PMID**: [35013434](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35013434/)
- **PMCID**: [PMC8748465](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/PMC8748465/)
- **来源链接**: [https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-021-04080-3](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-021-04080-3)
- **勘误**: DOI: [10.1038/s41598-024-52791-0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-52791-0)（2024 年 1 月 29 日）

> **说明**：以下正文基于可核验原文重写，所有方法、样本量、主要数值、局限性和结论均来自原文，未从题名或检索元数据推断全文事实。

---

## 摘要

**背景**：呼吸道合胞病毒（RSV）是儿童发病的主要原因之一，但由于临床中缺乏对住院呼吸道症状患儿的系统性 RSV 检测，现有报告发病率很可能低估了真实负担。

**目的**：开发一个预测模型，以估计西澳大利亚州（WA）5 岁以下住院儿童中 RSV 相关住院的真实发率，并计算基于实验室确认数据的漏查比率（under-ascertainment fraction）。

**方法**：利用概率关联的围产期、住院和实验室记录，纳入 2000—2012 年间出生于西澳大利亚州的 321,825 名儿童的住院数据。在有过 RSV 检测记录的住院儿童人群中拟合多变量 logistic 回归预测模型，预测因子基于有向无环图（DAG）和逐步向后选择从 27 个候选变量中筛选。通过十折交叉验证受试者工作特征曲线下面积（AUROC）评估模型预测性能，并使用校准带（calibration belt）和 Hosmer-Lemeshow 检验评估校准度。随后将模型应用于队列中所有住院记录，以获得预测的 RSV 住院发率，并与实验室确认的 RSV 入院发率进行比较。

**结果**：321,825 例住院中，37,784 例（11.7%）进行了 RSV 检测，阳性率为 22.8%（共 8,604 次阳性）。预测模型显示良好的区分能力（交叉验证 AUROC = 0.87，95% CI 0.86–0.88），灵敏度 58.4%，特异度 92.2%，阳性预测值 68.6%，阴性预测值 88.3%。3 月龄以下儿童的预测住院率为 43.7/1000 儿童年（95% CI 42.1–45.4），而基于实验室确认的相应发率为 31.7/1000 儿童年（95% CI 30.3–33.1）。RSV 阳性与更小的入院年龄（< 3 月龄，调整后比值比 AOR = 1.91）、男性、非原住民身份、急性毛细支气管炎诊断（AOR = 16.8）、较长住院时间等显著相关。

**结论**：基于现有实验室检测数据，RSV 住院的真实负担可能被低估 30%–57%。该模型可为 RSV 传播动力学模型提供输入参数，以更好地预测母体疫苗接种等预防措施的潜在效果。

---

## 引言

呼吸道合胞病毒是全球幼儿急性下呼吸道感染发病和死亡的主要原因之一，据估计每年导致 320 万例可检测到的住院 [Shi et al., Lancet 2017]。然而真实负担可能远高于此，约半数 RSV 相关死亡发生在医院之外。在澳大利亚，每 10 万名 5 岁以下住院儿童中估计有 418 例 RSV 相关病例 [Saravanos et al., MJA 2019]。本课题组前期基于西澳大利亚州（WA）人群的研究报告，5 岁以下儿童中 RSV 检出阳性住院率为 247/10 万儿童年，其中 3 月龄以下婴儿最高（28.1/1000 儿童年）[Moore et al., J Infect Dis 2020]。

一个核心问题是：在西澳大利亚州乃至全球多数地区，RSV 检测并未系统化开展，RSV 也未被列为法定报告疾病。前期研究显示，仅 10% 的 17 岁以下住院儿童在研究期间曾接受过 RSV 检测，且不同年份和年龄段之间的检测率差异显著；54% 因呼吸道感染住院的儿童缺乏相应的微生物检测 [Lim et al., Influenza Other Respir Viruses 2017]。因此，单纯依赖实验室检测数据估计 RSV 疾病负担，会引入严重的漏查偏倚。

随着抗病毒药物、母体疫苗和单克隆抗体等 RSV 防治手段陆续进入后期临床试验——以及 WHO 将 RSV 全球疾病负担估计列为优先事项——准确量化 RSV 负担对于推进免疫规划决策和建立疫苗效果评估基线至关重要。为此，本研究旨在：(1) 利用关联的行政卫生数据构建预测模型，识别住院儿童中 RSV 阳性的临床和人口学预测因子；(2) 应用此模型估计完整的 RSV 相关住院发率；(3) 量化基于实验室数据估计 RSV 负担的漏查比率。

---

## 方法

### 研究设计与数据来源

本研究为基于人群的回顾性队列研究，利用西澳大利亚州行政关联数据，纳入 1996—2012 年间该州所有出生登记，涵盖 321,825 名至研究期末不满 5 岁的住院儿童。数据来源包括：

- **围产期记录**：西澳大利亚州助产士通知系统（MNS），覆盖该州 > 99% 出生；
- **出生与死亡登记**；
- **住院记录**：医院发病率数据收集（HMDC），记录 2000 年 1 月 1 日至 2012 年 12 月 31 日期间所有 5 岁以下儿童的住院入院，含 ICD-10-AM 诊断编码；
- **实验室记录**：PathWest 实验室医学数据库，包含同一时期内呼吸道标本 RSV 检测结果。

通过西澳大利亚州数据关联分支机构进行概率关联。实验室标本采集日期在医院入院日期前后 48 小时内视为与当次住院关联的 RSV 检测。院内转科记录被合并为一次住院。

### 研究人群与样本量

源人群（用于构建预测模型）：在队列首 5 年内住院且拥有 RSV 检测记录的 37,784 次住院；排除 3,801 次有缺失项的记录后，33,983 次住院纳入最终预测模型拟合。

目标人群（用于估计 RSV 负担）：同期队列中所有不满 5 岁住院儿童，排除有缺失项的记录后共 321,825 次住院记录用于模型应用。

### 候选预测因子

从文献综述、课题组前期工作 [Moore et al., BMC Public Health 2010] 及临床合理性出发，初步选定 27 个候选预测因子。使用有向无环图（DAG）作为因果推断工具来确定最小充分调整变量集，包括：儿童年龄、性别、分娩方式（阴道顺产 vs. 剖宫产）、入院季节、原住民身份（通过验证算法定义）、母亲年龄、孕期吸烟（是/否）、社会经济地位（SES，基于 SEIFA 相对优劣势指数五分位）、同胞数量、胎龄（< 32 周、32–36 周、≥ 37 周）、入院年份、出生年份、住院时长（连续变量）、ICU 住院（是/否）、机械通气使用、母亲哮喘史，以及急性毛细支气管炎、肺炎、支气管炎、未特指急性下呼吸道感染、哮喘、上呼吸道感染、百日咳、流行性感冒等诊断编码。纳入出生季节和地理居住区域以考虑季节性和气候条件。最终模型还包含正弦和余弦函数项以捕捉 RSV 的季节性变异 [Stolwijk & Zielhuis, 1999; Edwards, 1961]。

### 模型开发与评估

采用多变量 logistic 回归，以 RSV 检测阳性为二分类结局变量。为调整同一儿童多次住院的相关性，使用稳健标准误。模型开发采用基于 AIC 的逐步向后选择法，移除的变量逐个重新插入以评估模型改进情况。

预测性能通过十折交叉验证 AUROC 曲线评估，采用 Stata `cvauroc` 命令计算各折 AUC 的均值，并使用自助法获取偏差校正的 95% 置信区间。以 0.5 作为概率截断值计算灵敏度、特异度、阳性预测值和阴性预测值。采用校准带（calibration belt）和 Hosmer-Lemeshow 拟合优度检验评估模型校准。灵敏度分析按实验室检测方法（免疫荧光法 vs. PCR）分层重复建模。所有分析使用 Stata v.16.0，DAG 图使用 DAGitty v2.3 制作。

### RSV 负担估计

将拟合的 logistic 回归模型应用于目标人群中所有无缺失变量的住院记录，计算每例住院的 RSV 阳性预测概率。以 0.5 为阈值，将预测概率 ≥ 0.5 的住院定义为 RSV 相关住院。采用生存分析技术计算预测 RSV 发率，以人-时间为分母（自出生至首次住院日期或删失日期），允许每人多次住院。

### 漏查比率的计算

定义为实验室确认 RSV 发率与预测 RSV 发率之间的差值。发率以每 1000 儿童年为单位报告，并按年龄组、入院年份、入院季节和出生月份分层。

### 报告规范与伦理

本研究遵循 TRIPOD 声明。获得西澳大利亚州卫生部人类研究伦理委员会和西澳大利亚州原住民健康伦理委员会的伦理批准；因使用去标识化关联数据，免于知情同意。

---

## 结果

### 队列特征

源人群中 321,825 名住院儿童共有 37,784 次（11.7%）住院进行了 RSV 检测。其中 8,471 例（22.4%）为 3 月龄以下婴儿，5,768 例（15.3%）为原住民。实验室确认 RSV 阳性共 8,604 次（22.8%）。RSV 阳性在年龄更小、非原住民、男性、母亲 SES 中等、居住在大都市区、以及南半球冬季（6—8 月）入院的儿童中更为常见。约三分之一（2,594 例）的 RSV 阳性住院发生在 3 月龄以下婴儿中；约四分之三的实验室确认 RSV 阳性儿童出院诊断为急性毛细支气管炎。

### 预测因子与模型性能

最终 logistic 回归模型纳入的变量包括：儿童年龄、性别、分娩方式、入院季节、原住民身份、母亲年龄、孕期吸烟、SES、同胞数量、早产、入院年份、出生年份、住院时长、ICU 住院、机械通气、母亲哮喘史、急性下呼吸道感染（ALRI）诊断码、其他感染诊断码，以及出生季节、地理居住区域和季节性正弦/余弦函数。

多变量分析显示，3 月龄以下（AOR = 1.91，95% CI 1.27–2.87）、非原住民（AOR = 1.44，95% CI 1.29–1.61）、有急性毛细支气管炎诊断（AOR = 16.8，95% CI 15.3–18.5）与 RSV 阳性显著正相关。来自偏远/农村地区、住院 3 天及以上、需使用机械通气的儿童 RSV 阳性概率亦升高。相反，早产、低 SES 和母亲哮喘史与 RSV 阳性率呈负相关。

十折交叉验证显示模型预测性能良好：**AUROC = 0.87（95% CI 0.86–0.88）**。灵敏度 58.4%（95% CI 57.3–59.6%），特异度 92.2%（95% CI 91.8–92.5%），PPV 68.6%（95% CI 67.5–69.7%），NPV 88.3%（95% CI 87.9–88.7%）。校准带显示模型校准良好，Hosmer-Lemeshow 检验不显著（*P* = 0.66），表明模型拟合优度满意。

### 实验室确认 vs. 预测 RSV 发率

预测发率在较小年龄组更高。3 月龄以下婴儿的预测 RSV 住院发率为 **43.7/1000 儿童年（95% CI 42.1–45.4）**，而实验室确认发率为 31.7/1000 儿童年（95% CI 30.3–33.1）。平均年 RSV 相关住院率：< 3 月龄为 404/1000 儿童年，3–6 月龄为 499/1000 儿童年，6–11 月龄为 302/1000 儿童年。

**漏查比率**估计：< 3 月龄为 **32%**，3–6 月龄为 **57%**，6–11 月龄为 **35%**。12 月龄以下婴儿占预测 RSV 住院的 76%，占估计漏查量的 39%。RSV 预测住院在冬季和 4—6 月出生的婴儿中达峰值。

### 时间趋势

预测 RSV 住院率在 2000—2012 年间每年第 26–29 周达峰，与实验室确认 RSV 住院的趋势一致，除 2007 年（第 34 周，66/1000 儿童年）和 2009 年（第 32 周，55.9/1000 儿童年）略有偏移。

---

## 讨论

本研究基于超过十年的全人群关联数据，构建了一个具有良好性能的 RSV 住院预测模型（AUROC = 0.87）。结果提示，基于实验室检测数据估计的 RSV 疾病负担至少被低估 **30%**，在某些年龄组别中漏查率可达 **57%**。这一发现对 RSV 疫苗和预防策略的公共卫生决策有重要意义，特别是作为传播动力学模型的输入参数。

通过与英格兰的类似研究比较，本模型的 AUROC（0.87）低于英格兰婴儿模型的 AUROC（0.90），但在特异度和阴性预测值上表现更优。差异可能源于研究人群和预测因子覆盖范围的不同。本模型纳入了围产期因素（如母亲年龄、孕期吸烟、胎龄、分娩方式），这在同类 RSV 预测研究中较为少见。

RSV 阳性最强的预测因子为急性毛细支气管炎的诊断编码（AOR = 16.8），其次为支气管炎和肺炎，这与英格兰的研究结果一致。值得注意的是，社会经济地位较低、早产和母亲哮喘史在本分析中与 RSV 阳性呈负相关，这与部分文献报道一致 [Reeves et al., J Infect 2019; Zar et al., Lancet Glob Health 2020]，且提示大多数 RSV 病例并无潜在基础合并症 [Hall et al., NEJM 2009]。非原住民和偏远/农村地区 RSV 住院率更高，可能与医疗可及性差异和家庭拥挤等因素有关。

### 研究局限性

1. **疾病严重程度范围受限**：模型基于住院记录与实验室检测前 48 小时内的关联数据，因此仅适用于需要住院的重症 RSV 感染，无法推断社区层面的 RSV 发病。急诊和社区 RSV 负担未被纳入。

2. **数据时限**：分析仅涵盖 2000—2012 年，最近 10 余年的住院趋势未被反映。然而，作者认为主要的围产期和环境预测因子的影响在时间上相对稳定，因此该模型在当代数据中仍然适用。

3. **预测因子缺失**：模型未纳入母乳喂养、免疫缺陷、日托以及在关联数据库中没有常规收集的环境变量等潜在预测因子。不过这些因素通常不被认为是 RSV 入院的强预测因子，其对模型估计的潜在影响预计有限。

4. **检测方法差异**：尽管检测方法本身不会影响接受检测的倾向，但敏感性分析提示不同检测方法（免疫荧光 vs. PCR）间模型性能略有差异。

5. **非原住民 RSV 高风险的解读**：研究观察到非原住民儿童的 RSV 住院阳性率高于原住民儿童，这一发现可能与检测模式、医疗系统的入院门槛等复杂因素有关，不必然等同于更低的 RSV 感染率。

6. **外部验证缺失**：模型仅进行了内部交叉验证，未在其他人群或地区中进行外部验证。开发简便的风险评分以促进临床转化和外部验证是今后研究的重要方向。

## 摘要

**背景**：呼吸道合胞病毒（RSV）是儿童发病的主要原因之一，但由于临床中缺乏对住院呼吸道症状患儿的系统性 RSV 检测，现有报告发病率很可能低估了真实负担。

**目的**：开发一个预测模型，以估计西澳大利亚州（WA）5 岁以下住院儿童中 RSV 相关住院的真实发率，并计算基于实验室确认数据的漏查比率（under-ascertainment fraction）。

**方法**：利用概率关联的围产期、住院和实验室记录，纳入 2000—2012 年间出生于西澳大利亚州的 321,825 名儿童的住院数据。在有过 RSV 检测记录的住院儿童人群中拟合多变量 logistic 回归预测模型，预测因子基于有向无环图（DAG）和逐步向后选择从 27 个候选变量中筛选。通过十折交叉验证受试者工作特征曲线下面积（AUROC）评估模型预测性能，并使用校准带（calibration belt）和 Hosmer-Lemeshow 检验评估校准度。随后将模型应用于队列中所有住院记录，以获得预测的 RSV 住院发率，并与实验室确认的 RSV 入院发率进行比较。

**结果**：321,825 例住院中，37,784 例（11.7%）进行了 RSV 检测，阳性率为 22.8%（共 8,604 次阳性）。预测模型显示良好的区分能力（交叉验证 AUROC = 0.87，95% CI 0.86–0.88），灵敏度 58.4%，特异度 92.2%，阳性预测值 68.6%，阴性预测值 88.3%。3 月龄以下儿童的预测住院率为 43.7/1000 儿童年（95% CI 42.1–45.4），而基于实验室确认的相应发率为 31.7/1000 儿童年（95% CI 30.3–33.1）。RSV 阳性与更小的入院年龄（< 3 月龄，调整后比值比 AOR = 1.91）、男性、非原住民身份、急性毛细支气管炎诊断（AOR = 16.8）、较长住院时间等显著相关。

**结论**：基于现有实验室检测数据，RSV 住院的真实负担可能被低估 30%–57%。该模型可为 RSV 传播动力学模型提供输入参数，以更好地预测母体疫苗接种等预防措施的潜在效果。

## 引言

呼吸道合胞病毒是全球幼儿急性下呼吸道感染发病和死亡的主要原因之一，据估计每年导致 320 万例可检测到的住院 [Shi et al., Lancet 2017]。然而真实负担可能远高于此，约半数 RSV 相关死亡发生在医院之外。在澳大利亚，每 10 万名 5 岁以下住院儿童中估计有 418 例 RSV 相关病例 [Saravanos et al., MJA 2019]。本课题组前期基于西澳大利亚州（WA）人群的研究报告，5 岁以下儿童中 RSV 检出阳性住院率为 247/10 万儿童年，其中 3 月龄以下婴儿最高（28.1/1000 儿童年）[Moore et al., J Infect Dis 2020]。

一个核心问题是：在西澳大利亚州乃至全球多数地区，RSV 检测并未系统化开展，RSV 也未被列为法定报告疾病。前期研究显示，仅 10% 的 17 岁以下住院儿童在研究期间曾接受过 RSV 检测，且不同年份和年龄段之间的检测率差异显著；54% 因呼吸道感染住院的儿童缺乏相应的微生物检测 [Lim et al., Influenza Other Respir Viruses 2017]。因此，单纯依赖实验室检测数据估计 RSV 疾病负担，会引入严重的漏查偏倚。

随着抗病毒药物、母体疫苗和单克隆抗体等 RSV 防治手段陆续进入后期临床试验——以及 WHO 将 RSV 全球疾病负担估计列为优先事项——准确量化 RSV 负担对于推进免疫规划决策和建立疫苗效果评估基线至关重要。为此，本研究旨在：(1) 利用关联的行政卫生数据构建预测模型，识别住院儿童中 RSV 阳性的临床和人口学预测因子；(2) 应用此模型估计完整的 RSV 相关住院发率；(3) 量化基于实验室数据估计 RSV 负担的漏查比率。

## 方法

### 研究设计与数据来源

本研究为基于人群的回顾性队列研究，利用西澳大利亚州行政关联数据，纳入 1996—2012 年间该州所有出生登记，涵盖 321,825 名至研究期末不满 5 岁的住院儿童。数据来源包括：

- **围产期记录**：西澳大利亚州助产士通知系统（MNS），覆盖该州 > 99% 出生；
- **出生与死亡登记**；
- **住院记录**：医院发病率数据收集（HMDC），记录 2000 年 1 月 1 日至 2012 年 12 月 31 日期间所有 5 岁以下儿童的住院入院，含 ICD-10-AM 诊断编码；
- **实验室记录**：PathWest 实验室医学数据库，包含同一时期内呼吸道标本 RSV 检测结果。

通过西澳大利亚州数据关联分支机构进行概率关联。实验室标本采集日期在医院入院日期前后 48 小时内视为与当次住院关联的 RSV 检测。院内转科记录被合并为一次住院。

### 研究人群与样本量

源人群（用于构建预测模型）：在队列首 5 年内住院且拥有 RSV 检测记录的 37,784 次住院；排除 3,801 次有缺失项的记录后，33,983 次住院纳入最终预测模型拟合。

目标人群（用于估计 RSV 负担）：同期队列中所有不满 5 岁住院儿童，排除有缺失项的记录后共 321,825 次住院记录用于模型应用。

### 候选预测因子

从文献综述、课题组前期工作 [Moore et al., BMC Public Health 2010] 及临床合理性出发，初步选定 27 个候选预测因子。使用有向无环图（DAG）作为因果推断工具来确定最小充分调整变量集，包括：儿童年龄、性别、分娩方式（阴道顺产 vs. 剖宫产）、入院季节、原住民身份（通过验证算法定义）、母亲年龄、孕期吸烟（是/否）、社会经济地位（SES，基于 SEIFA 相对优劣势指数五分位）、同胞数量、胎龄（< 32 周、32–36 周、≥ 37 周）、入院年份、出生年份、住院时长（连续变量）、ICU 住院（是/否）、机械通气使用、母亲哮喘史，以及急性毛细支气管炎、肺炎、支气管炎、未特指急性下呼吸道感染、哮喘、上呼吸道感染、百日咳、流行性感冒等诊断编码。纳入出生季节和地理居住区域以考虑季节性和气候条件。最终模型还包含正弦和余弦函数项以捕捉 RSV 的季节性变异 [Stolwijk & Zielhuis, 1999; Edwards, 1961]。

### 模型开发与评估

采用多变量 logistic 回归，以 RSV 检测阳性为二分类结局变量。为调整同一儿童多次住院的相关性，使用稳健标准误。模型开发采用基于 AIC 的逐步向后选择法，移除的变量逐个重新插入以评估模型改进情况。

预测性能通过十折交叉验证 AUROC 曲线评估，采用 Stata `cvauroc` 命令计算各折 AUC 的均值，并使用自助法获取偏差校正的 95% 置信区间。以 0.5 作为概率截断值计算灵敏度、特异度、阳性预测值和阴性预测值。采用校准带（calibration belt）和 Hosmer-Lemeshow 拟合优度检验评估模型校准。灵敏度分析按实验室检测方法（免疫荧光法 vs. PCR）分层重复建模。所有分析使用 Stata v.16.0，DAG 图使用 DAGitty v2.3 制作。

### RSV 负担估计

将拟合的 logistic 回归模型应用于目标人群中所有无缺失变量的住院记录，计算每例住院的 RSV 阳性预测概率。以 0.5 为阈值，将预测概率 ≥ 0.5 的住院定义为 RSV 相关住院。采用生存分析技术计算预测 RSV 发率，以人-时间为分母（自出生至首次住院日期或删失日期），允许每人多次住院。

### 漏查比率的计算

定义为实验室确认 RSV 发率与预测 RSV 发率之间的差值。发率以每 1000 儿童年为单位报告，并按年龄组、入院年份、入院季节和出生月份分层。

### 报告规范与伦理

本研究遵循 TRIPOD 声明。获得西澳大利亚州卫生部人类研究伦理委员会和西澳大利亚州原住民健康伦理委员会的伦理批准；因使用去标识化关联数据，免于知情同意。

---

## 结果

### 队列特征

源人群中 321,825 名住院儿童共有 37,784 次（11.7%）住院进行了 RSV 检测。其中 8,471 例（22.4%）为 3 月龄以下婴儿，5,768 例（15.3%）为原住民。实验室确认 RSV 阳性共 8,604 次（22.8%）。RSV 阳性在年龄更小、非原住民、男性、母亲 SES 中等、居住在大都市区、以及南半球冬季（6—8 月）入院的儿童中更为常见。约三分之一（2,594 例）的 RSV 阳性住院发生在 3 月龄以下婴儿中；约四分之三的实验室确认 RSV 阳性儿童出院诊断为急性毛细支气管炎。

### 预测因子与模型性能

最终 logistic 回归模型纳入的变量包括：儿童年龄、性别、分娩方式、入院季节、原住民身份、母亲年龄、孕期吸烟、SES、同胞数量、早产、入院年份、出生年份、住院时长、ICU 住院、机械通气、母亲哮喘史、急性下呼吸道感染（ALRI）诊断码、其他感染诊断码，以及出生季节、地理居住区域和季节性正弦/余弦函数。

多变量分析显示，3 月龄以下（AOR = 1.91，95% CI 1.27–2.87）、非原住民（AOR = 1.44，95% CI 1.29–1.61）、有急性毛细支气管炎诊断（AOR = 16.8，95% CI 15.3–18.5）与 RSV 阳性显著正相关。来自偏远/农村地区、住院 3 天及以上、需使用机械通气的儿童 RSV 阳性概率亦升高。相反，早产、低 SES 和母亲哮喘史与 RSV 阳性率呈负相关。

十折交叉验证显示模型预测性能良好：**AUROC = 0.87（95% CI 0.86–0.88）**。灵敏度 58.4%（95% CI 57.3–59.6%），特异度 92.2%（95% CI 91.8–92.5%），PPV 68.6%（95% CI 67.5–69.7%），NPV 88.3%（95% CI 87.9–88.7%）。校准带显示模型校准良好，Hosmer-Lemeshow 检验不显著（*P* = 0.66），表明模型拟合优度满意。

### 实验室确认 vs. 预测 RSV 发率

预测发率在较小年龄组更高。3 月龄以下婴儿的预测 RSV 住院发率为 **43.7/1000 儿童年（95% CI 42.1–45.4）**，而实验室确认发率为 31.7/1000 儿童年（95% CI 30.3–33.1）。平均年 RSV 相关住院率：< 3 月龄为 404/1000 儿童年，3–6 月龄为 499/1000 儿童年，6–11 月龄为 302/1000 儿童年。

**漏查比率**估计：< 3 月龄为 **32%**，3–6 月龄为 **57%**，6–11 月龄为 **35%**。12 月龄以下婴儿占预测 RSV 住院的 76%，占估计漏查量的 39%。RSV 预测住院在冬季和 4—6 月出生的婴儿中达峰值。

### 时间趋势

预测 RSV 住院率在 2000—2012 年间每年第 26–29 周达峰，与实验室确认 RSV 住院的趋势一致，除 2007 年（第 34 周，66/1000 儿童年）和 2009 年（第 32 周，55.9/1000 儿童年）略有偏移。

---

## 讨论

本研究基于超过十年的全人群关联数据，构建了一个具有良好性能的 RSV 住院预测模型（AUROC = 0.87）。结果提示，基于实验室检测数据估计的 RSV 疾病负担至少被低估 **30%**，在某些年龄组别中漏查率可达 **57%**。这一发现对 RSV 疫苗和预防策略的公共卫生决策有重要意义，特别是作为传播动力学模型的输入参数。

通过与英格兰的类似研究比较，本模型的 AUROC（0.87）低于英格兰婴儿模型的 AUROC（0.90），但在特异度和阴性预测值上表现更优。差异可能源于研究人群和预测因子覆盖范围的不同。本模型纳入了围产期因素（如母亲年龄、孕期吸烟、胎龄、分娩方式），这在同类 RSV 预测研究中较为少见。

RSV 阳性最强的预测因子为急性毛细支气管炎的诊断编码（AOR = 16.8），其次为支气管炎和肺炎，这与英格兰的研究结果一致。值得注意的是，社会经济地位较低、早产和母亲哮喘史在本分析中与 RSV 阳性呈负相关，这与部分文献报道一致 [Reeves et al., J Infect 2019; Zar et al., Lancet Glob Health 2020]，且提示大多数 RSV 病例并无潜在基础合并症 [Hall et al., NEJM 2009]。非原住民和偏远/农村地区 RSV 住院率更高，可能与医疗可及性差异和家庭拥挤等因素有关。

### 研究局限性

1. **疾病严重程度范围受限**：模型基于住院记录与实验室检测前 48 小时内的关联数据，因此仅适用于需要住院的重症 RSV 感染，无法推断社区层面的 RSV 发病。急诊和社区 RSV 负担未被纳入。

2. **数据时限**：分析仅涵盖 2000—2012 年，最近 10 余年的住院趋势未被反映。然而，作者认为主要的围产期和环境预测因子的影响在时间上相对稳定，因此该模型在当代数据中仍然适用。

3. **预测因子缺失**：模型未纳入母乳喂养、免疫缺陷、日托以及在关联数据库中没有常规收集的环境变量等潜在预测因子。不过这些因素通常不被认为是 RSV 入院的强预测因子，其对模型估计的潜在影响预计有限。

4. **检测方法差异**：尽管检测方法本身不会影响接受检测的倾向，但敏感性分析提示不同检测方法（免疫荧光 vs. PCR）间模型性能略有差异。

5. **非原住民 RSV 高风险的解读**：研究观察到非原住民儿童的 RSV 住院阳性率高于原住民儿童，这一发现可能与检测模式、医疗系统的入院门槛等复杂因素有关，不必然等同于更低的 RSV 感染率。

6. **外部验证缺失**：模型仅进行了内部交叉验证，未在其他人群或地区中进行外部验证。开发简便的风险评分以促进临床转化和外部验证是今后研究的重要方向。
